title: Pay Per Call Launch Checklist: 7 Checks Before Go-Live
h1: Pay per call launch checklist: 7 checks before sending live traffic
description: Use this pay per call launch checklist before sending live calls: buyer hours, caps, routing, compliance and test calls that stop costly mistakes.
faq: What should I check before sending live pay per call traffic?
Confirm the buyer's number, hours, daily cap and geography, write down what counts as a billable call, set a fall-back route, set affiliate payouts, and place test calls on every tracking number.
How do I test a pay per call campaign?
Call each tracking number yourself. Check that it reaches the right buyer, appears in the call log with the correct source and duration, and follows the fall-back path outside buyer hours.
Do I need a fall-back route in pay per call?
Yes. A fall-back destination means a call still goes somewhere when every buyer is closed, at their cap or blocked for that caller, instead of being dropped.
body:
A pay per call launch checklist is a short list of checks you finish before the first real customer dials your number: the number routes to the right buyer, the buyer's hours and caps are set, the rules for what counts as a billable call are written down, and a test call has proved all of it. Skipping the list means your first paying calls become your test calls.

Why a pay per call launch checklist matters

Live call traffic is expensive to waste. Every call that lands on a closed line, a buyer already at their cap, or a number with no recording notice is a call you cannot get back. Most of these problems are configuration mistakes, not bad luck, and they can all be caught with a few minutes of testing. If you have not yet built the campaign itself, start with our guide to pay per call campaign setup and come back here before you send traffic.

1. Agree the definition of a billable call

Before any technical work, write down what makes a call billable. The usual ingredients are a minimum duration, a rule for repeat callers and a rule for calls that never reach a person. Put the numbers in writing with the buyer and with each affiliate. Our article on minimum call duration rules explains the common choices. A rule that exists only in someone's head becomes a payout dispute later.

2. Confirm the buyer details

  • Destination number: dial it yourself and confirm a person answers.
  • Hours: set the days and times the buyer can take calls, including the time zone.
  • Daily cap: set the maximum number of calls the buyer will pay for per day.
  • Geography: list the states or countries the buyer wants, and what should happen to calls from elsewhere.
  • Payout: record the price per qualifying call.

3. Build the routing and the fall-back

Decide where a call goes when the first choice cannot take it. With waterfall routing, a call tries buyers in order and skips any that are closed, capped or blocked for that caller. Always have a last-resort destination, so a call is never dropped because every buyer said no. If you sell to several buyers, read how real-time bidding works to see whether it suits the campaign.

4. Check the compliance basics

Recording and calling rules differ by place and by vertical. Work out whether callers need a spoken recording notice, how do-not-call lists apply, and what each buyer requires. This is not legal advice: confirm your obligations with your own counsel before you go live. Vertical pages such as insurance and legal show the kind of rules to ask about.

5. Set up affiliate numbers and payouts

Give each affiliate or traffic source its own tracking number so every call can be traced to where it came from. Set each partner's payout rate before launch, and agree when statements are sent. Changing rates after calls have started is the fastest way to lose a partner's trust.

6. Place test calls

Call every tracking number from a phone you control. Check that:

  1. The call rings the intended buyer and the line is clear.
  2. The call shows up in your call log with the right source and duration.
  3. Calling outside the buyer's hours takes the fall-back path.
  4. A repeat call from the same number is handled the way you decided.
  5. Any recording notice plays when it should.

7. Switch on monitoring and alerts

Decide in advance how you will know something is wrong. Watch for a spike in very short calls, a buyer hitting their cap early, or a source sending calls from places you do not serve. Quality grading helps here: see call quality scoring for how sources can be graded and paused when they send too many short calls.

How the checklist works in Insight Dial

Insight Dial covers most of these steps inside the platform. The guided setup checklist walks you through the campaign, and the test-call tool lets you place a call before real traffic arrives. You set buyer hours, daily caps, state rules, blocked numbers and repeat-caller blocks in the routing rules, with a pre-transfer check before a call is passed on. Dynamic number insertion and per-source tracking numbers tie each call to its source, and per-affiliate payout rates feed downloadable statements. Spoken recording notices can be switched on where rules need one, and alerts can go to Slack, Discord, Teams or WhatsApp. Quality grades of Good, Watch and Poor help you spot weak sources, and sources sending too many short calls can be paused automatically. See call tracking features for the detail and pricing for how pay-as-you-go billing works.

A final read-through

Before you send traffic, read the whole setup once as if you were the caller and then as if you were the buyer. If anything surprises you, fix it first. A calm, boring launch is the goal.
